Zach Lahn

Republican candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Iowa · Open seat

Farmer and business investor

Zach Lahn is a farmer and business investor from Belle Plaine, Iowa, and this is his first run for office. He earlier worked as a political staffer in Colorado, Montana and Iowa and for Americans for Prosperity. He entered the race in November 2025 and won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary for governor with about 37.7% of the vote, beating U.S. Rep. Randy Feenstra and other candidates. His running mate is Derek Wulf.

Where Lahn stands

Property taxes
Says his long-term goal is to eliminate property taxes on primary residences, arguing that people 'shouldn't have to rent your home from the government.'
Local control
In the first general-election debate, said local governments should have more control over decisions affecting their communities.
Taxes
Supports more tax cuts made in a fiscally responsible way.
Housing and out-of-state investors
Proposes lowering property taxes by raising rates on 'Wall Street investors' and banning hedge funds from buying single-family homes.
Economic development
Proposes sending state economic development money to Iowa-owned companies instead of out-of-state or foreign corporations.
Data centers
Argues that property taxes are the main long-term benefit of hosting a data center in Iowa and that the state is giving that benefit away.
K-12 education
Says the problem for Iowa's public schools is burdensome regulation and argues that schools need more innovation.
Education savings accounts (ESAs)
Supports third-party auditing of private schools that take ESA funds; his campaign said he wants 'truly independent audits' to protect taxpayer dollars.
Abortion
Describes himself as 'unapologetically pro-life at conception' and says that position also covers healthier food, less medication for children and clean water.
Agriculture and monopolies
Says breaking up monopolies was first done by Republicans and calls for clean water. Has campaigned on reducing the influence of large corporations in agriculture and pharmaceuticals.

Background

  • Republican nominee for Iowa governor, 2026 (won June 2, 2026 primary)

  • Former political staffer in Colorado (including for a state senator), Montana and Iowa
